name: Saints Peter and Paul Basilica
history: The parish was founded in January 1852. A stone church begun in 1858 was nearly finished when the Civil War stopped work; in 1863, around the Battle of Chickamauga, the Union Army seized it and used its stone for fortifications and culverts. The present church was dedicated on 29 June 1890. It became a basilica in 2011.
arch: Red-brick Gothic Revival with a tall central tower and spire. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
features: Its stained glass, designed by Louis Comfort Tiffany, shows the life of St. Peter on the east side and St. Paul on the west.
A Kilgen organ was built for the church in 1936.

look.d: The brick spire rises over downtown Chattanooga.
Peter's life on one side, Paul's on the other.

fun: An earlier church on the site was dismantled by the Union Army for its stone.
journal: An army took the first church apart. The second one has Tiffany glass.
